messages:
maria: Customer reported intermittent 401s when connecting to SSE stream. Only happens when they supply a signed cookie + an Authorization header. Customer provided request id rqd-9f4b7a2c and time range ~2026-03-17T14:25:30Z -> 14:27:10Z. Asking ops for repro steps we can validate and a minimal curl.
kevin: Can you paste the exact endpoint they hit and the sample headers (sanitized)? Also which region/route and whether they're behind a corporate proxy.
ingrid: For repro let's collect: 1) full request headers (use --dump-header), 2) curl with -N/--no-buffer, 3) whether removing cookie or auth header changes behavior. Try cookie-only, header-only, both.
maria: Endpoint: https://api.redwood.prod/streaming/v1/chat?route=default-usw2
Model: rw-instruct-3b (streaming SSE)
Region: us-west-2
Customer said their proxy may be mutating cookies. They gave these request ids: rqd-9f4b7a2c, rqd-9f4b7a2f (both same minute).
Sanitized curl I asked them to run (replace <TOKEN> and <SIGNED_COOKIE>):
```
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Cookie: session=<SIGNED_COOKIE>" \
  --dump-header headers.txt \
  "https://api.redwood.prod/streaming/v1/chat?route=default-usw2"\
```
Ask them to attach headers.txt and the stdout. Also asked them to include --trace-ascii trace.txt if they can.
support-bot: Ticket #54421 updated: awaiting customer debug bundle. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
samir: I'll try to validate locally. Two quick things: 1) curl sometimes reuses cookies from cookie-jar; ensure no ~/.curlrc is setting cookies. 2) Use --no-keepalive? (not needed yet)
kevin: Also add a test with an explicit empty Cookie header to ensure proxy isn't adding one: `-H "Cookie:"` or `-H "Cookie: "` depending on curl version. And run with `-i` to show response status line and any 401 body.
maria: Customer returned headers.txt and stdout. They show an initial HTTP/1.1 200 OK with SSE lines but after ~18s the connection drops and our logs show a 401 for the followup request trying to re-auth. Customer segment of headers.txt (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: rqd-9f4b7a2c

event: message
data: {"chunk":"hello"}

# later connection closed by server
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
content-length: 86
x-request-id: rqd-9f4b7a2f
{"error":"unauthenticated","msg":"cookie signature invalid"}
```
kevin: That log snippet suggests the runtime accepted the initial request (200) then later tried to validate something and switched to cookie validation and failed. Might be an auth precedence bug (header wins initially but background refresh validates cookie?).
ingrid: From infra side, if client reconnects or we attempt background token refresh and cookie is present, our middleware currently checks cookie signature even if Authorization header was valid. Can you get us proxy logs (if they have one) and full server ingress logs with the trace id? We need the exact TCP connection events.
maria: I pulled logs from the ingress for rqd-9f4b7a2c window: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:25:33Z] rqd-9f4b7a2c conn=ab12 accept, auth=header_ok
[2026-03-17T14:25:36Z] rqd-9f4b7a2c sse: chunk_sent
[2026-03-17T14:25:51Z] rqd-9f4b7a2c background: auth_check cookie_present sig_invalid
[2026-03-17T14:25:52Z] rqd-9f4b7a2f conn=ab12 respond 401 cookie signature invalid
```
This looks like a background validation path is treating the cookie as authoritative and failing.
samir: I ran a quick matrix locally. Commands I used (replace placeholders):
```
# header only - works (keeps streaming)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $LIVE_TOKEN" "https://.../streaming/v1/chat?route=default-usw2"

# cookie only - 401 if cookie unsigned/expired
curl -N -H "Cookie: session=$EXPIRED_COOKIE" "https://.../streaming/v1/chat?route=default-usw2"

# both header + expired cookie - intermittent 200 then 401 (repro)
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $LIVE_TOKEN" -H "Cookie: session=$EXPIRED_COOKIE" "https://.../streaming/v1/chat?route=default-usw2"
```
I see the same pattern: initial stream + chunk then 401. I can repro without the customer's proxy.
kevin: Good repro. Sounds like a server-side bug where cookie validation runs on a timer/refresh path and fails the connection even when header-based auth should persist for the lifetime of the connection. Raise to eng-runtime.
ingrid: Filing internal bug: ENG-RUNTIME-1289. Root cause hypothesis: background session validation routine doesn't check for active header-based session context. I'll attach logs and samir's repro.
maria: To help debugging/forensics we need the customer to run one more sanitized curl and upload the headers + trace output. Ask them: run the exact command below (paste with redacted placeholders) and upload headers.txt + trace.txt to the ticket. Also ask them to include the raw stdout from curl (it will contain SSE messages).
```
# reproducible command to run and attach outputs
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Cookie: session=<SIGNED_COOKIE>" \
  --dump-header headers.txt \
  --trace-ascii trace.txt \
  "https://api.redwood.prod/streaming/v1/chat?route=default-usw2" > stdout.txt
# attach headers.txt trace.txt stdout.txt to ticket
```
support-bot: Customer uploaded bundle -> s3://redwood-support-bundles/54421/1955554321-bundle.tar.gz
maria: OK received. @ingrid @kevin I've attached the bundle to the bug. Samir, can you validate the bundle and confirm whether the ingress behavior matches your local repro?
samir: Validating now. Quick note: when re-running with `-H "Cookie:"` (explicit empty header) the connection stays healthy. That strongly indicates cookie presence triggers the failing path. I'll add my validation steps to ENG-RUNTIME-1289 and include the curl logs.
kevin: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to implement guard so cookie background validation doesn't terminate header-authenticated SSE connections. 2) ops to add a temporary mitigation: prefer header auth if Authorization header present on initial connection. 3) ask customer to omit cookie or use header-only until fix is rolled.
maria: I'll send the mitigation note to the customer and add the temporary workaround. Thanks everyone, moving to bug triage. :pray:
